issues.title: Test file separated from component
issues.description: The rule requires that for every React component file component.tsx, the test file component.test.tsx exists in the same directory. However, the test file schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx was placed in a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located

issues.title: Drag-and-drop reordering swaps source and target indices
issues.description: The handleDragEnd function passes arguments to moveItem in the wrong order - it calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead of moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). This causes drag-and-drop operations to place items in the opposite position from where they're dropped. For example, dragging an item from index 2 to index 0 will incorrectly move the item at index 0 to index 2 instead, creating confusing and incorrect reordering behavior for users.

issues.title: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context
issues.description: The sortableKeys array is constructed from all localKeyedValues instead of excluding prefix items. The code removed the .slice(prefixItemsCount) operation, meaning prefix items (which should have fixed positions and not be draggable) are now included in the SortableContext. This allows prefix items to be moved via drag-and-drop, violating the constraint that prefix items must remain in their fixed positions and breaking the schema's structural requirements.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)
const sortableKeys = localKeyedValues.map((item) => item.key);

issues.title: Unused local variable `prefixItemsCount` added
issues.description: `prefixItemsCount` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the component. This leaves unused code in the codebase, violating the rule requiring unused items to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20223 - Add drag-and-drop reordering for schema form arrays
pr.author: Unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds drag-and-drop reordering to the schema form's array editor using @dnd-kit. Each non-prefix item gets a GripVertical drag handle (in schema-form-input-array-item.tsx), and schema-form-input-array-list.tsx wraps the list in a DndContext with pointer and keyboard sensors and a SortableContext. Prefix (tuple) items get a placeholder instead of a handle. The existing Move up/down menu items are kept.

The rendering and wiring look reasonable, but the drop handler is broken. handleDragEnd calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex), and moveItem(from, to) takes its arguments in the opposite order, so a drag moves the wrong item. Drops onto prefix slots are also allowed, which can put a regular item into a tuple position. The tests added are four snapshot renders. None of them exercise dragging, moveItem, or the move menu, even though the PR description claims behavioral tests exist.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The core feature does not work. Dragging item A onto position C in [A,B,C] produces [C,A,B] instead of [B,C,A], so users get reorderings they did not ask for and the wrong values are written back through onValuesChange. The drop handler also lets regular items land in tuple slots. Both need fixing before merge, and a test that actually performs a reorder should be added.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, SchemaFormInputArrayList (ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx) owns a local keyed copy of the array values in React state. Each row, SchemaFormInputArrayItem, renders the value through SchemaFormInput and a dropdown menu with Delete, Move up and Move down. Those menu actions call moveItem(from, to), which splices the local list and pushes the new values to the parent through onValuesChange. Tuple (prefixItems) positions are fixed by index and cannot move.

This PR adds a dnd-kit layer on top of that structure. The list wraps its rows in a DndContext with pointer and keyboard sensors, and a SortableContext keyed by each row's uuid. Each row calls useSortable and attaches its listeners to a new drag-handle button. Dragging ends in handleDragEnd, which converts the dragged and dropped keys to indices and then calls moveItem. Because moveItem expects (from, to) and the drag code passes (newIndex, oldIndex), the reorder is applied backwards.
steps: Entry point: SchemaFormInputArrayList holds localKeyedValues, keyed by uuid, and derives the prefix-versus-regular split from property.prefixItems.
The new DndContext and SortableContext wrap all rows. sortableKeys currently includes every row, including the prefix rows.
Each row in SchemaFormInputArrayItem calls useSortable({ id: itemKey, disabled: !canMove }) and attaches the listeners only to the new GripVertical button when canMove is true.
On drop, handleDragEnd finds the old and new indices and calls moveItem. That call has the arguments reversed (see the first finding).
moveItem splices the local state and calls onValuesChange. The menu's Move up and Move down actions reuse this same function, so the fix belongs in the drag handler and not in moveItem.
Test coverage is four snapshot renders in schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx. No test covers the reorder logic or the prefix constraint.

findings.title: Drag-and-drop moves the wrong item because moveItem arguments are reversed
findings.fixPrompt: In ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx, handleDragEnd (around lines 130-145) calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex). moveItem(from, to) expects the source index first, so the call is reversed and drags move the wrong row. Change it to moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). Keep the existing -1 guards. Add a test that performs a real reorder through the drag-end path and asserts the resulting values order, so this regression is caught.

findings.title: Regular items can be dropped into tuple (prefixItems) slots
findings.fixPrompt: In ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx, the sortableKeys list (around line 148) includes prefix (tuple) rows, so regular items can be dropped into prefix positions. Build sortableKeys from the non-prefix rows only, using prefixItemsCount (around line 45) to slice off the prefix entries. Also make sure handleDragEnd ignores any drop whose target index is below prefixItemsCount, as a defensive check. Follow the existing getCanMoveForIndex logic for what counts as a prefix row. Add a test confirming that a regular item cannot be moved into a prefix slot.

findings.title: PR description claims behavioral tests that are not in the diff
findings.fixPrompt: The PR description says behavioral tests exist for move up/down and for prefix items being immovable, but ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx (the array describe block, around lines 489-551) only contains snapshot renders. Add behavioral tests in the same file or a new schema-form-input-array-list test file. They should: (1) render a three-item string array, trigger 'Move up' and 'Move down' from the row menu, and assert the resulting values order; (2) simulate a drag-end with @dnd-kit (or by calling the list's reorder path) and assert the order; (3) assert that a prefix row has no drag handle and that a regular item cannot be reordered into a prefix slot. Assert on the resulting values passed to onValuesChange, not on internal calls.

findings.title: Menu Move up can move a regular item into a tuple slot (pre-existing, now more visible)
findings.fixPrompt: In ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-item.tsx, the Move up menu item (around lines 112-114) is shown when canMove && !first. first is only true for index 0, so the first non-prefix row can move up into a prefix slot. Change the visibility condition so Move up is hidden when the row above is a prefix row. The simplest approach is to pass a canMoveUp boolean from SchemaFormInputArrayList (true when index - 1 >= prefixItemsCount) and use it in place of !first. Match the existing getCanMoveForIndex pattern in schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.

findings.title: Dead prefixItemsCount and a misleading comment in the list component
findings.fixPrompt: In ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form-input-array-list.tsx, prefixItemsCount (around lines 45-47) is declared but never used, and the comment above sortableKeys (around line 147) says the keys are for non-prefix items while the code maps over all rows. Once the drop-target fix is applied, prefixItemsCount will be used to slice sortableKeys, so the variable and comment become accurate. If that fix is not applied, delete the unused variable and correct the comment to match the actual behavior.

findings.title: Snapshot IDs depend on test order and the enum test does not cover drag
findings.fixPrompt: In ui-v2/src/components/schemas/schema-form.snapshot.test.tsx, the array snapshots include dnd-kit generated IDs (DndDescribedBy-N, DndLiveRegion-N) that depend on the order tests run in the file. Replace the brittle snapshots with assertions on the drag handle's aria-label, role, and tabindex, or pass a stable id to DndContext so the IDs do not shift. Also rename or remove the with enum items test, since it does not render the drag path. Regenerate the snapshot file only after the changes.

findings.title: Drag handle and dnd-kit wiring are structured cleanly
findings.body:
Good choices here:

- useSortable is called with disabled: !canMove, so prefix rows never register as draggable, and the handle is only rendered for regular rows.
- The KeyboardSensor uses sortableKeyboardCoordinates, which gives keyboard reordering and matches dnd-kit's documented pattern.
- The <div className="w-5" /> placeholder keeps the grid aligned for prefix rows, so rows line up whether or not they have a handle.
- The drag handle uses text-muted-foreground and hover:text-foreground, semantic tokens that work in light and dark mode.
- The menu Move up and Move down actions are kept as the non-pointer fallback.
